title: Lightweight CNN-Based Artifact Reduction for Scientific Error-bounded Lossy Compression
problem: Lossy compression widely used for large-scale scientific data but introduces artifacts that compromise analysis. Error-bounded compressors (SZ, ZFP) provide tight control but artifacts remain visible. Need post-processing method to improve reconstruction quality without excessive overhead.
motivation: Scientific applications require error bounds for reproducibility, but compression artifacts (e.g., blocking, oscillation) degrade utility. Deep learning offers opportunity for efficient artifact reduction, but must maintain fast inference and generalize across compressors/datasets.
method: The method uses a lightweight 3D neural network to remove distortions left by lossy compression. Training uses fixed-scale batch normalization—a technique that standardizes input data at each layer using a consistent scale—to keep training stable and inference fast. The researchers measured how network size affects output quality (minimum MSE loss, or average squared error from correct values) and validated the approach across five compressors (SZ1, SZ2, SZP, SZX, ZFP) and multiple scientific domains.
key_novelty: This is the first systematic study of using neural networks to remove compression distortions from scientific data, with demonstrated success across five compressors (SZ1, SZ2, SZP, SZX, ZFP) and multiple scientific domains.
contributions: Lightweight 3D CNN architecture for artifact reduction
Fixed-scale batch normalization for stable training/inference
Empirical analysis of network size vs. MSE tradeoff

metrics.generalization: Single-file training generalizes to other files in same dataset

limitations: Abstract only - no specific datasets named, no comparison with other artifact-reduction methods (e.g., other post-processing networks), unclear applicability to extreme compression ratios
primary_theme: Deep learning for improving lossy compression quality
